title: Production Application UI
outcome: Build a production application shell and reusable UI states instead of isolated demo components.
artifact: TaskFlow responsive shell with navigation, workspace context, task screens, loading/empty/error states, and accessible interactions.
labSteps: Design the application shell first: sidebar/topbar/main content/mobile navigation.
Create reusable primitives for page header, panel/card, empty state, loading skeleton, and error state.
Build workspace/board/task navigation with active state derived from routing rather than duplicated local state.
Compose Server and Client Components so interactive islands remain small.
Test keyboard focus, labels, landmarks, reduced-motion expectations, and narrow widths.
Exercise all non-happy states by forcing no data, slow data, error, and forbidden responses.
failureModes: Global client component wrapping the whole app
Mobile layout treated as desktop squeezed smaller
mastery: Can compose a shell from reusable patterns
Can verify basic accessibility and responsive behavior
principles: Build production UI from reusable layout and interaction patterns, not a collection of one-off pages.
Represent loading, empty, error, success, and permission states explicitly.
Accessibility and responsive behavior are requirements of the component, not a final polishing step.
Keep UI composition separate from server-state ownership so components remain understandable.

quiz.question: Which practice best matches Phase 20's engineering goal?
options: Build production UI from reusable layout and interaction patterns, not a collection of one-off pages.
Use broad permissions and public access first, then harden later.
Add abstractions before a concrete problem requires them.
Hide failures by returning the same success/status shape for every outcome.
quiz.explanation: Build production UI from reusable layout and interaction patterns, not a collection of one-off pages.
